solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Angry, beak finding weapon

parts.note: cross means angry, as in a cross word
the bow is the front of a ship, its beak or prow

explanation.surface: An angry bird finds its beak is a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beak' suggests a bird or a magistrate, but here it is the projecting front of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbow is a mechanical bow firing bolts, a type of weapon.

clue.text: Hit and run, being negligent

parts.note: to slap is to hit with an open hand
a dash is a short run

explanation.surface: A hit-and-run driver is accused of negligence.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash work is careless and hurried, the mark of someone negligent.

clue.text: What may make CID honest?

parts.note: the clue's CID is made by putting ... together, so reading the joining in words gives the solution

explanation.surface: A question of what could make the police detectives truthful.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police; 'What may make' asks what produces those three letters: C and ID.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone candid is frank and truthful, so the word is a synonym for honest.

clue.text: Adaptable electric current feeding factory

indicators.note: one piece feeding another goes inside it

parts.note: a plant is an industrial factory
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Electricity is supplied to a flexible factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Pliant means flexible and easily bent or influenced, hence adaptable.

clue.text: German playwright's second terrifying work

parts.note: a chiller is a frightening book or film

explanation.surface: A German dramatist's second piece is a horror story.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after playwright stands for 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Schiller was the German dramatist who wrote William Tell and Mary Stuart.

clue.text: Data acquiring university prestige

indicators.note: the data figures acquire, or take inside, the university letter

parts.note: stats, short for statistics, are data

explanation.surface: Figures show a university gaining prestige.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is standing or rank in society, the same idea as prestige.

clue.text: Distinctive clothing, note, I brought into special sports meeting

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: the letter I is brought into the meeting, placing it inside

parts.note: a gala is a special sports event, as in a swimming gala

explanation.surface: Someone takes a musical note into a sports day while wearing ceremonial dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Regalia are the distinctive emblems and robes of office or rank.

clue.text: Elegance shown by good people

parts.note: a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: Elegance is displayed by worthy folk.
explanation.definitionFit: Grace is smooth elegance of movement or manner.

clue.text: Petition about it after oil's spilt

indicators.note: after places the pieces that follow behind the scrambled ones
spilt suggests the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: the possessive gives the letters of oils
C, from circa, means about
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone lodges a petition over an oil spill.
explanation.definitionFit: To solicit is to ask earnestly for something, which is to petition.

clue.text: One following singular speaker

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a talker is someone who speaks

explanation.surface: A follower seems to be one particular orator.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalker is a person who follows another obsessively.

clue.text: Impish youngster, beginning to swagger, theatrically exaggerated

indicators.note: the start of swagger supplies just its first letter

parts.note: camp means affected and theatrically overdone

explanation.surface: A cheeky child starts to swagger in an overdone, stagey way.
explanation.definitionFit: A scamp is a mischievous child, a rascal or imp.

clue.text: Scriptwriter having tipple with performer right away

parts.note: a dram is a small drink of spirits

indicators.note: right away means the right letter goes, deleted from the performer

parts.note: an artist can be a performer

explanation.surface: A writer has a drink with an actor, who then leaves immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: A dramatist writes plays, so is a scriptwriter for the stage.

clue.text: Street band likes playing for idle amusement

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are moved around and rearranged

explanation.surface: A busking street band would like to perform just for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' looks like music from the band, but it signals rearranging the letters of STREET BAND LIKES.
explanation.definitionFit: Life is not all beer and skittles: the idiom means leisure and pleasure, mere amusement.

clue.text: Show about the climate

indicators.note: the show word goes about, around, the other piece

parts.note: to wear something is to display or show it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A television programme about climate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show' looks like a TV show, but it is the verb, as in wearing a smile.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather is the short-term state of the atmosphere, loosely the same as climate.

clue.text: Deserter in a potty situation

parts.note: a po is a chamber pot, a potty
a state is a condition or situation

explanation.surface: A deserter finds himself in a crazy predicament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potty' reads as crazy, but it is the noun: a po.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostate abandons their faith or party, so is a deserter of it.

clue.text: Savoury dish produced by boy, eaten by libertine

indicators.note: being eaten by places the boy inside the libertine

parts.note: a roue is a debauched man, a libertine
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A rake devours a youth, producing a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A roulade is a rolled dish, often of meat or a savoury filling.

clue.text: Judge a person willing to provide a testimonial

definitions.meaning: an official who rules on play in sport

definitions.text: a person willing to provide a testimonial
definitions.meaning: someone who vouches for a job applicant's character

explanation.definitionFit: A referee both officiates a match and gives a reference for an applicant.

clue.text: Highwaymen following, so adopt changes

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in pp. and ff.

indicators.note: changes indicates the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: After this, someone decides to switch to a new practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Footpads were robbers on foot who held up travellers, akin to highwaymen.

clue.text: Disgustingly loaded, having gold deposited — here?

definitions.text: Disgustingly loaded, having gold deposited — here?

indicators.note: the gold is deposited within the scrambled letters
disgustingly hints at the letters being messed up

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: A place where the filthy rich have gold put away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disgustingly' reads as moral disgust at wealth but signals reordering; 'deposited' puts the gold inside. The whole clue also describes the legendary city.
explanation.definitionFit: The fabled city of gold, where everyone would be disgustingly rich.

clue.text: Realm of fantasy provided by castles in Spain?

definitions.meaning: an imaginary ideal world of daydreams
daydreams or impossible schemes, like castles in the air

explanation.definitionFit: Unrealistic dreamers are said to live in this imaginary place, from Aristophanes' Birds.

clue.text: Yellow head of cage bird

indicators.note: the head of the word is its first letter

parts.note: a raven is a large black bird

explanation.surface: A caged bird with a yellow head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yellow' looks like a colour describing the bird, but it means cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Craven means cowardly, the slang sense of yellow.

clue.text: County circle upset staff at first

indicators.note: at first places the turned staff word before the circle
in a down clue, upset turns the staff word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick
a set is a social circle

explanation.surface: A county's group overturns the officials' decisions initially.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' turns ROD into DOR. DORSET is a county in southwest England.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorset is an English shire, an example of a county.

clue.text: To stay the course means working

parts.note: one's keep is one's means of livelihood
on means working or operating

explanation.surface: Persevering is a matter of continuing to work.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep on is to continue or persist, staying the course.

clue.text: Some of what's eaten on a cruise ship?

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Passengers consume some of the food on a cruise.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sailing on a cruise ship is out on the ocean, away from land.

clue.text: Take turns to change a ten, counterfeit

parts.note: to alter is to change

indicators.note: counterfeit suggests falsifying, so the letters are remade in another order

explanation.surface: Two crooks take turns changing a fake ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: To alternate is to do things by turns, one after the other.

clue.text: Ask compiler, ultimately, for puzzle

parts.note: to pose a question is to ask it

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of compiler

explanation.surface: A request for the setter to provide a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is a difficult question, a puzzle.

clue.text: Very serious furthest from the centre

explanation.definitionFit: Extreme means both drastic in degree and outermost in position.

clue.text: Getting on one in crazy game

parts.note: someone getting on in years is old

indicators.note: in places the one inside the crazy word

parts.note: mad means crazy
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An ageing person who is a little crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting on' and 'crazy' paint a person; the definition is a children's card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Maid is a card game in which the loser holds the unmatched card.
